appliedObject.name: Hadeland Glassverk
appliedObject.finding: The stable named Hadeland Glassverk point remains the correct semantic anchor for the complete production, museum and visitor institution.

officialVisitorContext.sourceName: Hadeland Glassverk – opening hours and visitor information
officialVisitorContext.finding: The current official visitor page identifies a living experience centre with production viewing, museum, activities, shops and dining, all subject to changing opening schedules.

officialAreaMap.finding: The official map treats Glasshytta, museum, shops, dining and other visitor functions as components of one named glassworks environment.

officialIndustrialIdentity.finding: The official history identifies the glassworks as founded in 1762 at Jevnaker by Randsfjorden and describes the development from bottles and household glass to design and art glass.

productionCoreContext.finding: The official site calls Glasshytta the heart of the operation and documents continuing glassblowing, grinding and polishing. No stable separately named building geometry was captured, so the institution anchor is retained instead of inventing a Glasshytta centroid.

areaCrossCheck.name: Hadeland Glassverk
areaCrossCheck.finding: The named park polygon confirms the wider public environment but cannot represent the living industrial institution alone.

independentEntityCrossCheck.finding: Wikidata independently identifies Hadeland Glassverk as a glassworks and company founded in 1762 at Jevnaker.

contractDecision.finding: The source object and coordinate remain correct; the previous semantic labels were outside the Coordinate Source Contract v1 enum and are replaced with valid institutional-area anchor values.

radiusDecision.finding: The retained radius covers the central production, museum, park and visitor environment without claiming a property, heritage, production, safety or access boundary.

decision.representationLimit: The marker represents the named glassworks institution and central visitor-production complex. Glasshytta, the museum, park, retail buildings and dining venues remain components.
